elements.element: Vendor has an express duty to defend Customer and its affiliates.
elements.evidence: Revised 16.2 reads "Array shall defend, indemnify and hold harmless each of Ono, its Affiliates and Sublicensees and the directors, officers and employees of Ono, its Affiliates and Sublicensees" — an express defence duty running to Ono and its Affiliates (and Sublicensees).

elements.element: Vendor indemnifies Customer and its affiliates against third-party claims.
elements.evidence: Retained 16.2 chapeau: indemnity "from and against any and all Liabilities from any Third Party Claims incurred by any Ono Indemnitee", with Ono Indemnitees defined to include Ono, its Affiliates and Sublicensees.

elements.element: Vendor indemnity covers claims that Services or Deliverables infringe intellectual property rights.
elements.evidence: New 16.2(e): "any claim that any Product infringes or misappropriates the intellectual property rights of a Third Party". In this licence the Product is the contract subject matter standing in for services/deliverables, and the cover is unqualified. The deterministic check "vendor indemnity for IP infringement present = false" is a phrasing artefact (it appears keyed to "Services or Deliverables"); on substance the IP indemnity is present in the rendered operative text.

elements.element: Vendor indemnity covers Vendor's breach of applicable law.
Vendor indemnity covers a data breach caused by Vendor.
elements.evidence: New 16.2(g): "any unauthorized access to or disclosure of Ono's Confidential Information caused by Array" — unauthorised access/disclosure of Customer-side information caused by Vendor.

elements.element: Vendor indemnity covers Vendor's gross negligence and wilful misconduct.
elements.evidence: New 16.2(h): "Array's gross negligence or willful misconduct"; the retained tail excludes only claims resulting from an Ono Indemnitee's own gross negligence/wilful misconduct, which does not cut back (h).

elements.element: The indemnification procedure requires notice of a claim.
elements.evidence: 16.3 (unchanged): Indemnitee "shall promptly notify the other Party (the 'Indemnitor') in writing of any Third Party Claim".

elements.element: The indemnification procedure allocates control of the defence.
elements.evidence: 16.3: "the Indemnitor shall have sole control of the defense and/or settlement thereof", subject to keeping the Indemnitee informed and settlement-consent limits.

elements.element: The indemnification procedure requires reasonable cooperation.
elements.evidence: 16.3: "The Indemnitee under this Section 16.3 shall cooperate fully with the Indemnitor and its legal representatives in the investigation of any action with respect to a Third Party Claim covered by this indemnification."

elements.element: Customer indemnity is limited to Customer-provided content and Customer's breach of law.
elements.evidence: 16.1 as revised is limited to "(a) materials, data or content provided by Ono to Array under this Agreement; and (b) Ono's breach of applicable Law"; the former commercialization, clinical-study/product-liability and Article 15 prongs are removed.

elements.element: Vendor indemnifies Customer against third-party intellectual-property claims.
elements.evidence: New 16.2(e) covers "any claim that any Product infringes or misappropriates the intellectual property rights of a Third Party".

elements.element: The IP indemnity may exclude infringement caused by Customer modifications.
elements.evidence: Permissive element; no modification exclusion was inserted, which is more favourable to Customer than the fallback allows, so the condition does not bite.

elements.element: The IP indemnity may exclude infringement caused by Customer combinations.
elements.evidence: Permissive element; no combination exclusion inserted — the indemnity is broader than the fallback permits, so nothing to fail.

elements.element: The IP indemnity may exclude infringement caused by Customer specifications.
elements.evidence: Permissive element; no Customer-specification exclusion inserted, which is Customer-favourable.

elements.element: Vendor must procure continued use, modify, or replace the infringing item.
elements.evidence: No procure/modify/replace remedy ladder appears anywhere in revised Article 16; 16.2(e) is a pure indemnity.

elements.element: Vendor must refund applicable fees if procure, modify, or replace remedies are unavailable.
elements.evidence: No refund-of-fees backstop is drafted in the rendered language.

elements.element: Vendor's indemnity is subject to a super-cap of three times annual fees.
elements.evidence: No 3x annual fees super-cap (or any cap reference) is added to Article 16 in the rendered text.

reasons: Preferred level is complete on the operative text: 16.2 now carries an express defence duty, IP infringement (e), breach of Law (f), unauthorised access/disclosure of Ono Confidential Information (g) and gross negligence/wilful misconduct (h), while retained 16.3 already supplies notice, sole control of the defence and full cooperation, and 16.1 is narrowed to Ono-supplied materials plus Ono's breach of Law.

The deterministic signal "vendor indemnity for IP infringement present = false" is not borne out in substance — new 16.2(e) is an express third-party IP infringement/misappropriation indemnity. The regex appears keyed to "Services or Deliverables" wording, which does not exist in this pharma licence; "Product" is the correct contract analogue.

Fallback is not satisfied (no procure/modify/replace ladder, no refund backstop, no 3x super-cap), but that is immaterial because the preferred checklist is complete; the fallback need not be reached.

Minimality holds: the additions to 16.2 are the four missing preferred coverage heads plus the single word "defend", and the deletions in 16.1 are exactly what the "Customer indemnity limited to Customer-provided content and Customer's breach of law" element requires. No survival tail, expense language, extra damages categories or boilerplate was added, and the favourable retained carve-outs and 16.3 procedure are untouched.

Intent is preserved on the rendered text: the retained 16.2(a)-(d), the Products Liability Claim defined term, the Indemnitee/Indemnitor mechanics and the settlement-consent and notice-prejudice sentences all survive without contradiction, and no cross-reference is left dangling.

Repair point to raise before sending, not a checklist failure: the rationale itself notes Section 11.4 leaves each Subject Party to defend Infringement Actions "at its own expense". If 11.4 covers defence of third-party infringement claims (as opposed to enforcement of the parties' own patents), add "Notwithstanding Section 11.4" at the head of 16.2(e) so the new IP indemnity is not read down by that retained sentence.

Drafting nit for the comment, not the operative text: the margin note should also flag that Ono's product-liability and Article 15 indemnity prongs were deleted, since a counterparty reading only the comment ("narrowed Ono's indemnity to Ono-supplied materials and Ono's breach of Law") may not appreciate that the reciprocal clinical-study allocation has gone; the rationale's offer to restore it if the IP indemnity is granted is the right trade.
